newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL says Sky announcement likely soon.
newsitem.headline: INL says Sky announcement likely soon.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd is likely to make an announcement this month on whether it has secured a signficant stake in New Zealand pay-TV operator Sky Network Television, Managing Director Mike Robson said on Tuesday.

"The next time we make an announcement it will be (that) we're either going ahead or we're not going ahead," Robson said. "I think that we're at the stage where we will know that soon, but rather than drip-feeding out where we are, I'd sooner just say we're still discussing aspects of it and next time we say something it'll be conclusive."
Asked when the announcement would be made, Robson replied: "It'll be nearer the end of the month."
In October last year INL said it was negotiating with a group of companies that together own more than 80 percent of Sky to buy a substantial stake.

Those companies include Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corporation (8.8 percent), Tappenden Construction (7.7 percent) and United States-based HKP Partners (51.1 percent). HKP is partly owned by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, which in turn own half of Telecom Corp of New Zealand.
State-owned Television New Zealand holds the balance of Sky, but that stake is not for sale.
INL had hoped to seal the Sky deal by the end of December, but later set back any announcement to January because of "tedious detail".
INL is 49.5 percent owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation. Sky is not related to Murdoch's 40 percent-owned European-based satellite network BSkyB.
